description: Media for the What's On TV public demo server (demo.whatsontv.net). Every item is CC-BY (attribution required, see credits.html) or in the US public domain. Researched 2026-11-22; see README.md for the basis per item and for titles that were considered and left out.

items.title: Big Buck Bunny
items.basis: The Peach open movie project's results are licensed CC-BY 3.0 by the Blender Foundation; the full credits roll must stay in the film when it is screened or broadcast whole.
items.notes: Source is the official Blender download mirror (download.blender.org itself sits behind a Cloudflare browser challenge). The separately released score is CC-BY-NC-ND, but the film as a whole is CC-BY 3.0.

items.title: Elephants Dream
items.basis: The Orange open movie project released the film under the Creative Commons Attribution license, with this exact credit line for redistribution.
items.attribution: (c) copyright 2006, Blender Foundation / Netherlands Media Art Institute / www.elephantsdream.org
items.notes: 1080p DivX master on Internet Archive; video.blender.org only offers 720p. The separately distributed soundtrack files are CC-BY-NC-ND 2.5, but the film is CC-BY.

items.title: Sintel
items.basis: The Durian open movie project's results are licensed CC-BY 3.0; redistributing the movie requires keeping the entire credits scroll.

items.title: Tears of Steel
items.basis: The Mango open movie project's results are licensed CC-BY 3.0 by the Blender Foundation.
items.notes: The standalone soundtrack files are CC-BY-ND 3.0 ((C) Joram Letwory - www.tearsofsteel.org); played unaltered inside the film they need no extra permission, but don't extract or remix the music.

items.title: Cosmos Laundromat
items.basis: The Gooseberry open movie project's work is licensed CC-BY 3.0 by the Blender Foundation.
items.notes: Source is Blender's own PeerTube (video.blender.org), 1920x804. Some third-party copies label it CC-BY 4.0; the project's own page says 3.0.

items.title: His Girl Friday
items.basis: Columbia's 1940 copyright (reg. L 9305) was not renewed, so the film entered the US public domain in 1969, and the underlying 1928 play The Front Page entered the public domain on 1 January 2024.
items.notes: Use this original-release transfer only, not a colorized version or a studio restoration (new restoration work can carry its own claims). A 2025 security agreement (V15039D155) recorded at the Copyright Office lists this title; it is a financing record, not a renewal, but see README.

items.title: Meet John Doe
items.basis: Frank Capra Productions' 1941 copyright (reg. L 10453) was not renewed in its 28th year, so the film fell into the US public domain in 1969.
items.notes: 1990s registrations by Annahold BV and Evergreen Entertainment (PA0000607538, PA0000700261) cover their restored or colorized editions only; this source is the original black-and-white release.

items.title: The Stranger
items.basis: The Haig Corporation registered the film in 1946 (reg. L 409) but did not renew the copyright in 1973, so it is in the US public domain.
items.notes: Use this older transfer, not MGM's 2004 restoration.

items.title: D.O.A.
items.basis: The copyright renewal for D.O.A. was invalid (the Copyright Office first recorded an invalid renewal and later corrected its error), so the film is in the US public domain.
items.notes: Wikipedia cites David P. Hayes, 'Copyright Office Records an Invalid Renewal, Then Corrects Its Error' (Copyright Registration and Renewal Information Chart, 2008). The film premiered in December 1949 and went on general release in 1950; TMDB lists it as 1950.

items.title: The Little Shop of Horrors
items.basis: Roger Corman never secured copyright for the film, so it entered the US public domain on release.
items.notes: Wikipedia cites Fishman, The Public Domain (Nolo, 5th ed. 2010), and Pierce, 'Forgotten Faces', Film History 19:2 (2007). The 1982 stage musical and the 1986 film are separate copyrighted works and aren't involved.

items.title: Carnival of Souls
items.basis: The US release prints of Carnival of Souls lacked a valid copyright notice, which put the film in the US public domain.
items.notes: Wikipedia cites Rapold, 'Even Good Films May Go to Purgatory', The New York Times, 2014-02-14. Use the US theatrical cut from this source, not a later director's cut or restoration.

items.title: The First Forty Days in Korea
items.basis: The Big Picture was produced by the US Army Signal Corps (Army Pictorial Service), and as a work of the US government it was never eligible for copyright (17 U.S.C. 105).
items.notes: NARA local ID 111-TV-169. Part of the first 13-episode Korean War run broadcast on CBS in late 1951 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Big_Picture_(American_TV_series)). Episode numbers here follow NARA order, not an official numbering.

items.title: The Case of the Cunningham Heritage
items.basis: The episode was syndicated in the US in 1954, and the Copyright Office's online records (which hold every renewal filed from 1978, including the 1981-83 window this episode needed) show no renewal for it; all of Conan Doyle's Holmes stories are public domain in the US as of 1 January 2023.
items.notes: Searched 2026-11-22 for the episode title: the only hit is a 2025 security agreement (V15039D155), with no RE renewal record. Guild Films production starring Ronald Howard, filmed in France and first published in US syndication. Source is 640x360.
